speaker: C1/3

text: You have never looked more charming than you do tonight Dorian. You remind me of the day I saw you first. I wish you would tell me your secret. To get back my youth I would do anything in the world, except take exercise, get up early, or be respectable.
speaker: Lord H

text: I have changed Harry. I have done too many dreadful things in my life.  I am not going to do any more.  I began my good actions yesterday.
speaker: Dorian

text: Where were you yesterday?
speaker: Lord H

text: In the country.
speaker: Dorian

text: My dear boy anybody can be good in the country.  There are no temptations there. (To audience) He listened with an amused smile as Dorian tried to describe his transformation for a full twenty minutes.
speaker: Lord H

text: He was bored within seconds.
speaker: Chorus

text: Tick tock
speaker: Chorus

text: Hetty is not one of our own class, of course.  But I really loved her.  I am quite sure that I loved her.  All during this wonderful May I have ridden down to see her every week. Yesterday she met me in a little orchard. We were to have gone away together this morning at dawn. Suddenly I determined to leave her as flowerlike as I had found her.
speaker: Dorian

text: I should think the novelty of the emotion must have given you a thrill of real pleasure. So you broke this girl’s heart?
speaker: Lord H

text: Harry, you are horrible! Hetty's heart is not broken.   Of course, she cried. But there is no disgrace upon her. She is unharmed.
speaker: Dorian

text: Do you think this girl will ever be content with anyone of her own rank now?  From a moral point of view, I cannot say that I think much of your great renunciation.  She will despise any husband and be wretched. And you bask in the glow of your goodness.
speaker: Lord H

text: Oh Harry!  You mock at everything. I am sorry I told you now. Don't tell me that the first bit of self-sacrifice I have ever shown, is really a sort of sin.  How can we be friends if you don’t believe I’ve changed?
speaker: Dorian

text: You cannot change in my eyes, Dorian and you and I will always be friends.
speaker: Lord H

text: Yet you poisoned me with a book.  Harry, promise me that you will never lend that book to anyone. It does harm.
speaker: Dorian

text: My dear boy, don’t moralise. You and I are what we are, and will be what we will be.  The books that the world calls immoral are books that show the world its own shame.
speaker: Lord H

text: You are wrong Harry but I am too tired to argue.
speaker: Dorian

text: He could not rest after Lord Henry left.
speaker: Chorus

text: A new life!  That was what he wanted.
speaker: Chorus

text: Surely he had begun it already.  He had spared Hetty.
speaker: Chorus

text: He would never again tempt innocence. He would be good.
speaker: Chorus

text: He thought of the portrait that carried all his sins
speaker: Chorus

text: Perhaps the signs of evil had already gone away.
speaker: Chorus

text: He took the lamp from the table and crept upstairs.  Yes, he would be good, and the hideous thing that he had hidden away would no longer be a terror to him.
speaker: Dorian

text: He dragged the purple hanging from the portrait.
speaker: Chorus

text: A cry of pain broke from him.
speaker: Chorus

text: The painting had changed
speaker: Chorus

text: But his wish had been perverted

text: The mouth was more twisted.
speaker: Chorus

text: The eyes more cunning
speaker: Chorus

text: The thing was still loathsome.

text: More loathsome than before.

text: Had there been nothing more in his renunciation than Vanity?  Curiosity?  Hypocrisy?

text: There must be something more to his one good deed.

text: His noble sacrifice.
